words.meaning: Imperfect (inchoative) middle of macomai, to fight in armed combat (#Ac 7:26), then to wage a war of words as here and #2Ti 2:24. They were already murmuring (#Jo 6:41), now they began bitter strife with one another over the last words of Jesus (#43-51), some probably seeing a spiritual meaning in them. There was division of opinion about Jesus in Jerusalem also later (#7:12,40; 9:16; 10:19). (Robertson's NT Word Pictures)
words.plain: Strove [Greek: emachonto] — the word originally meant fighting in armed combat, then came to mean waging a war of words. The crowd wasn't just puzzled by what Jesus said — they broke into heated argument with each other, some taking his words literally, some sensing something deeper. This kind of division followed Jesus everywhere [see John 7:12, 40; 9:16; 10:19].
